comparisons.peer_topic: Ten-for-one forward stock split execution and share count adjustment
comparisons.peer_summary: On July 12, 2024, the company completed a ten-for-one forward stock split, increasing authorized common stock from 2.9 billion to 29 billion shares without changing the $0.001 par value per share.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom executed significant common stock capital events in fiscal year 2024. Intel's disclosure focuses on the secondary sale of converted shares from its Mobileye investment, specifically converting 38.5 million Class B shares to Class A and selling them for net proceeds of $1.6 billion. In contrast, Broadcom executed a ten-for-one forward stock split, which increased authorized common stock from 2.9 billion to 29 billion shares but did not generate direct cash proceeds like Intel's offering. While both actions alter the share structure and potentially dilute existing holdings or adjust par values/authorized limits, Intel's event was a liquidity transaction involving specific non-controlling interest shares, whereas Broadcom's was a structural split of its own common stock.

sentences.text: During 2023, we converted 38.5 million of our Mobileye Class B shares into Class A shares, representing 5% of Mobileye's outstanding capital stock, and subsequently sold the Class A shares for $42 per share as part of a secondary offering, receiving net proceeds of $1.6 billion and increasing our capital in excess of par value by $663 million, net of tax.

On July 12, 2024, we completed a ten-for-one forward stock split of our common stock, proportionately increasing the number of shares of our authorized common stock from 2.9 billion to 29 billion without changing the par value of $0.001 per share.
